item.title: Garden Pathway Repair
item.description:
Before

The garden path was uneven, overgrown, and difficult to navigate after rain. The old stones had shifted, making it hard to carry tools or move safely through the space.

After

We repaired and reset the path using new materials and a low-maintenance edging system. The finished route is level, easy to sweep, and visually tied to the planting beds around it.

The Story

The goal was not just to fix the path, but to make it feel like part of the landscape. We chose materials that complement the yard and built a route that supports gardening routines instead of interrupting them.

item.title: Coastal Bathroom Refresh
item.description:
Before

The existing bathroom felt dark and dated, with old tile, a small vanity, and limited storage. The fixtures were mismatched and the room did not reflect the home’s coastal setting.

After

We refreshed the space with crisp white tile, a floating wood vanity, and a touch of texture in the shower niche. New lighting and a refined color palette make the room feel bright, calm, and intentional.

The Story

This refresh was all about making every inch count. We improved storage with built-in shelves, swapped the tub for a glass-walled shower, and chose finishes that are both timeless and durable for a high-humidity environment.

item.title: Big L Desk
item.description:
Problem

This project redesigned a space from a makeshift desk into a multifunctional workspace. Day job on the left, hobby on the right. No more competing for real estate or unnecessary barriers to entry.

Design

  • Birch plywood for the top and trim.
  • Plywood edges left exposed to let the material “be what it is.”
  • 4x4 pine legs, cleaned up on the table saw and sanded to 220 grit.
  • Finished with 3 coats of satin polyurethane.

item.title: Craftsman Walk in Closet
item.description:
Before

The existing closet was a cramped reach-in with low shelving and wasted vertical space. Clothes were stacked, and there was no easy place for shoes, linens, or daily outfits.

After

We turned the space into a walk-in closet with a craftsman feel: built-in drawers, open shelving, and a dedicated dressing nook. Rich wood tones and matte black hardware make it feel more like a room than a closet.

The Story

We framed the closet with a borrowed light and redesigned the interior layout for easy access. Each shelf and drawer was sized for the client’s wardrobe, and the new layout makes getting ready faster and more enjoyable.

item.title: Outdoor Gazebo Shower
item.description:
Before

There was a small, unfinished corner behind the house that was perfect for a backyard shower, but it lacked privacy, drainage, and a cohesive look.

After

The finished space is a comfortable outdoor shower wrapped in cedar, with a rain shower head, stone floor, and a fence that keeps the area private while still letting air and light in.

The Story

We built the gazebo structure from the ground up, making sure the framing, waterproofing, and drainage all worked together. The finished shower is both practical after beach days and beautiful enough to be a destination in the yard.

item.title: Mid Century Slat Wall
item.description:
Before

After

The Story

Whoever built this house thought it was a good idea to plant a porch pillar right between the dining room and living room. Structurally necessary, but visually, an eyesore.

The client had always loved slat walls, and this was the perfect opportunity. Rather than hiding the pillar, we made it the centerpiece.

Each slat was sanded down to a final 240 grit, smooth enough to take stain evenly and feel finished to the touch. We sampled several stains before landing on Gunstock, a warm brown with just enough red undertone to complement the room’s existing palette. The final coat, a clear satin polyurethane, gives off a subtle reflectivity in low light that makes the wall feel alive in the evening.

item.title: Bluestone Patio
item.description:
Before

After

The Story

This project was all about defining and connecting spaces.

The backyard had untapped potential, but getting from the back door to the garage meant crossing patchy grass — and on rainy days, that meant dragging mud into the house. There was no real place to sit outside, no reason to linger.

Natural bluestone was the answer. Beautiful and functional in equal measure, it created a hardscape that works as both a living space and a practical path between structures. The stone is laid to carry water away from both buildings, where it used to pool during heavy rains.
